methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable components, and ensuring that each component represented a distinct aspect of the counter's functionality or implementation.
spec_atomic_units: Module has synchronous active-high reset input (reset)
Output q changes only on the rising edge of clk
When reset is high, the output q will be 0 on the next rising edge of clk
When reset is low, the output q increments by 1 on each rising edge of clk, wrapping around from 15 to 0
Combinational logic determines the next state of q
If reset is asserted (high), the next state of q is 4'b0000
If reset is not asserted (low), the next state of q is the current state of q incremented by 1
Increment operation wraps around from 4'b1111 to 4'b0000
4-bit adder is required to increment the current value of q
Multiplexer selects between the reset value (4'b0000) and the incremented value
The register q is updated using a non-blocking assignment (<=)
